Quick note after the QBR: our ingestion pipelines are going to spike in mid-June and we need a short-term surge lane plus clarity on the renewal for Q3. Current monthly token spend is ~14M but projections (see attached internal forecast) show a potential 3–4x increase for two weeks during a campaign.

Can you share a short performance readout (latency, tail-p90/p99, and token reconciliation) and a recommended capacity/term option? Procurement will need a ballpark for the contract addendum before their monthly board review.

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. Looping Ben (Customer Solutions) and Laura (Renewals lead) to pull the performance metrics and draft options.

High-level plan:
- We’ll produce a one-page performance snapshot (p50/p90/p99, avg token latency) plus token reconciliation for the last 30/90 days.
- Provide two surge options: a) 2-week burst credits (prepaid) with no term change, b) 3-month staged uplift (discounted committed capacity) with a 6–9 month addendum and SLA bump.
- Include cost + ROI model showing unit cost delta vs hosted baseline and expected latency retention at increased throughput.

Can you confirm whether Trellis needs a guaranteed latency SLA for the surge window (e.g., p95 < 400ms)? If procurement wants the term amendment, we can attach a proposed addendum draft for their legal review.

I’ll send the snapshot and the proposed term PDF by Wednesday EOD.

Cheers,

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Q2 renewal & surge capacity request — performance snapshot attached

Alex / Jasmine — attaching the token-level report and an ROI workbook with assumptions. Highlights from infra ops review:

- Baseline (last 30 days): 14.1M tokens/mo; p50=62ms, p90=210ms, p99=580ms (small tail due to cold KV shards).
- When scaled to projected peak (approx 45M tokens/day burst): we recommend a dedicated burst lane (N+2 GPU set) + prefix/KV caching warmup script. Expected p90 to stay < 350ms, p99 ~650ms if cache warms correctly.
- Cost estimate: 2-week prepaid burst credits ~$35k (net of standard discount). 3-month committed uplift (50% Add-on) reduces token unit cost by ~28% over baseline; recommended for customers running sustained >20M tokens/mo post-burst.
- Risk & mitigations: quantization-friendly model variant reduces memory pressure (small quality delta — A/B tested on subset), and we recommend enabling prefix cache in the first 24 hours of the campaign to avoid initial tail spikes.

Action items I will own: attach perf graphs and a short runbook for the warmup script (included in trellis_q2_token_report.pdf). Laura — I’ve included a proposed term addendum draft (proposed-term-addendum-draft.pdf) with sliding discount tiers.

-ben
Ben Carter
Customer Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attached: trellis_q2_token_report.pdf; roi_model_v2.xlsx

Thanks team — this is really helpful. A few notes from our side after internal review: 

- Procurement prefers the 3-month staged uplift (makes the board comfortable) but wants the addendum to cap spend at the upper 90% projected line; they also requested a short pilot milestone to validate latency during Week 1 of the campaign.
- Legal will need the addendum with a clear rollback clause if latencies exceed p95 450ms for more than 4 hours total.
- Can you confirm whether the prefix/KV warmup script requires us to route traffic through a special endpoint or if it can be executed from our existing integration? (If special endpoint, we need runbook and temporary credentials.)

Requesting: final addendum PDF with the spend cap language and the Week 1 pilot plan by Friday so procurement can include it in the board packet. Also please include a one-paragraph summary I can paste into the procurement memo (cost, latency guardrail, expected ROI).

If you want, we can do a quick 20-min call Friday morning to finalize language.

Appreciate it — Alex
Head of ML Ops, Trellis.ai
